Title: {Accessing the Life in Smoke: A New Application of Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) to Sample Wildland Fire Bioaerosol Emissions and Their Environment}
Claim_Boundary: Demonstrates UAS collection of viable microorganisms and environmental measurements in smoke above wildland fires. Supports the bounded claim that fire-specific UAS plume sampling has been demonstrated without implying end-to-end response effectiveness.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: MDPI Fire open-access full text and USDA Forest Service record (DOI 10.3390/fire2040056). No manuscript change was required.

Title: {Advancing the community health vulnerability index for wildland fire smoke exposure.}
Claim_Boundary: Develops a county-level wildland-fire-smoke Community Health Vulnerability Index for CONUS using exposure sensitivity and adaptive-capacity components and documents spatial disparities. Supports the manuscript's community vulnerability and response-capacity synthesis but not personalised clinical prediction.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: PubMed and ScienceDirect publisher records (PMID 37839481; DOI 10.1016/j.scitotenv.2023.167834). No manuscript change was required.

Title: {Air quality policy and fire management responses addressing smoke from wildland fires in the United States and Australia}
Claim_Boundary: Reviews the historical development and interaction of wildland-fire smoke-management and air-quality policy in the United States and Australia and discusses implications for other fire-prone countries. Supports the manuscript's fire-specific policy context without demonstrating an AI governance control.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: International Journal of Wildland Fire publisher full text (DOI 10.1071/WF16154). No manuscript change was required.

Title: {An empirical model to estimate daily forest fire smoke exposure over a large geographic area using air quality, meteorological, and remote sensing data.}
Claim_Boundary: Builds an empirical daily wildfire-smoke PM2.5 model from monitoring meteorology fire and satellite inputs for populated areas of British Columbia and assigns estimates to local health areas for surveillance. It supports area-level population exposure estimation but not individual mobility time-activity indoor infiltration occupation or protective behaviour.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Partial correction required. Source route: Nature open-access full text and PubMed/PMC records (PMCID PMC3994508; PMID 24301352; DOI 10.1038/jes.2013.87). The corresponding manuscript wording/attribution correction was applied: In the health-interface paragraph explicitly separate area-level ambient/exposure assignment supported by this study from personal-exposure determinants supported by other sources.

Title: {Assessing the Risk of Respiratory-Related Healthcare Visits Associated with Wildfire Smoke Exposure in Children 0-18 Years Old: A Systematic Review.}
Claim_Boundary: Systematic review specifically assesses respiratory symptoms and healthcare visits among children aged 0--18 after wildfire-smoke exposure and identifies children as a susceptible group. Supports the manuscript's bounded paediatric-health synthesis.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: MDPI/PubMed open full text (PMID 34444546; DOI 10.3390/ijerph18168799). No manuscript change was required.

Title: {Building a Practice-Based Research Agenda for Wildfire Smoke and Health: A Report of the 2018 Washington Wildfire Smoke Risk Communication Stakeholder Synthesis Symposium.}
Claim_Boundary: Reports a 2018 Washington stakeholder synthesis involving 76 participants from more than 30 organisations and identifies practice-based needs barriers and solutions for wildfire-smoke risk communication and risk reduction. Supports the manuscript's claims about operational users trusted relationships ownership and communication implementation without validating AI alerts.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: MDPI/PubMed full text plus University of Washington symposium report (PMID 31284542; DOI 10.3390/ijerph16132398). No manuscript change was required.

Title: {Chemical Tomography in a Fresh Wildland Fire Plume: A Large Eddy Simulation (LES) Study}
Claim_Boundary: Uses a high-resolution WRF large-eddy simulation coupled to chemistry and airborne observations to study three-dimensional chemical evolution and cross-plume heterogeneity in a fresh wildland-fire plume. Supports the manuscript's claim that high-resolution 3-D models can resolve vertical/chemical structure omitted by simpler representations at greater computational cost.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: AGU open full text plus NOAA/NASA repository copies (DOI 10.1029/2021JD035203). No manuscript change was required.

Title: {Community Health and Resilience Under Rising Wildfire Smoke Exposure: A Review of Social Vulnerability and Adaptive Capacity}
Claim_Boundary: Narrative integrative review links wildfire-smoke health effects with social vulnerability and adaptive capacity including socioeconomic resources housing quality healthcare access risk communication safe indoor environments and affordability of protective measures. Supports the manuscript's response-capacity and equity synthesis while remaining review-level evidence.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: MDPI open-access full text and indexed abstract (DOI 10.3390/su18115380). No manuscript change was required.

Title: {Development and Evaluation of a North America Ensemble Wildfire Air Quality Forecast: Initial Application to the 2020 Western United States “Gigafire”}
Claim_Boundary: Develops and evaluates a North American multi-model ensemble wildfire-air-pollution forecast using regional and global chemical-transport models against satellite AOD and AirNow PM2.5 during the 2020 western US fires. Supports its classification as a concentration/air-quality forecast without implying universal superiority.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: AGU full text plus NOAA repository record (DOI 10.1029/2022JD037298). No manuscript change was required.

Title: {Differences in the Estimation of Wildfire-Associated Air Pollution by Satellite Mapping of Smoke Plumes and Ground-Level Monitoring.}
Claim_Boundary: Compares satellite smoke-plume-density categories with PM2.5 from 16 Bay Area ground monitors during the 2017--2018 California wildfire seasons and finds substantial spatial/temporal mismatch including unknown plume vertical position. Supports cross-platform measurement limitations and the need to combine sources; it does not itself establish satellite revisit latency.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported with wording boundary. Source route: MDPI/PMC open full text and PubMed record (PMCID PMC7663802; PMID 33167314; DOI 10.3390/ijerph17218164). The corresponding manuscript wording/attribution correction was applied: When revising the operational-constraints paragraph attribute spatial/temporal and vertical-representation mismatch to this paper rather than a generic hours-to-days latency claim.

Title: {Effect modification of the association between fine particulate air pollution during a wildfire event and respiratory health by area-level measures of socio-economic status, race/ethnicity, and smoking prevalence.}
Claim_Boundary: Examines effect modification of wildfire-event PM2.5 respiratory-health associations by area-level socioeconomic status race/ethnicity and smoking prevalence. It supports differential vulnerability and stratification but does not directly establish household filtration transport healthcare communication or financial response capacity.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Partial correction required. Source route: IOP publisher record/full text and bibliographic abstract (DOI 10.1088/2752-5309/acc4e1). The corresponding manuscript wording/attribution correction was applied: Move this citation to the susceptibility/vulnerability statement or qualify the response-capacity paragraph so the detailed resource list is supported chiefly by the adaptive-capacity reviews.

Title: {Efficacy of Communication Techniques and Health Outcomes of Bushfire Smoke Exposure: A Scoping Review.}
Claim_Boundary: Scoping review synthesises bushfire-smoke health effects and communication recommendations and reports that age rurality geography cultural/linguistic background and disability affect information needs or channels. Supports the manuscript's communication/intervention interface at review level without proving health-outcome efficacy.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: MDPI/PMC open full text and PubMed record (PMCID PMC8536189; PMID 34682636; DOI 10.3390/ijerph182010889). No manuscript change was required.

Title: {Engaging interested parties to optimize wildfire smoke communication in Canada: challenges with initiating change.}
Claim_Boundary: Evaluates a Canadian wildfire-smoke communication workshop and summary report using follow-up surveys; documents intended and reported organisational changes plus barriers including limited staff time resources remit and reversion to established processes during live events. Supports the manuscript's organisational ownership/capacity and stakeholder-participation claims.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: Frontiers/PMC open full text (PMCID PMC10652752; DOI 10.3389/fpubh.2023.1268249). No manuscript change was required.

Title: {Evaluation of Model-Based PM2.5 Estimates for Exposure Assessment During Wildfire Smoke Episodes in the Western U.S.}
Claim_Boundary: Evaluates multiple model-based PM2.5 products against observations during western-US wildfire-smoke episodes to assess spatial and temporal exposure-estimation performance. It supports model-based ambient exposure surfaces and their uncertainty but not individual mobility indoor infiltration occupation activity or protective behaviour.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Partial correction required. Source route: PubMed/PMC and ACS publisher records (PMCID PMC10288567; PMID 36693177; DOI 10.1021/acs.est.2c06288). The corresponding manuscript wording/attribution correction was applied: In the health-interface paragraph use this source for ambient/model-based exposure estimation and reserve personal-exposure determinants for sources that measured or modelled them.

Title: {Evaluation of Turbulence Depending Drag Coefficient in Plume Rise Model for Fire Smoke Dispersion}
Claim_Boundary: Evaluates a turbulence-dependent drag coefficient in a Lagrangian plume-rise model against prescribed-fire observations and examines resolution dependence. It supports the manuscript's task-dependent vertical-structure and resolution trade-off but not operational performance for uncontrolled wildfires.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported with wording boundary. Source route: Elsevier publisher abstract and indexed source record (DOI 10.1016/j.atmosenv.2024.120411). No manuscript change was required.

Title: {Health benefits and costs of filtration interventions that reduce indoor exposure to PM2.5 during wildfires.}
Claim_Boundary: Models six residential filtration interventions for a ten-day Southern California wildfire-smoke period and estimates indoor-exposure reduction health benefits and costs. This directly supports classifying it as a tested fire-specific intervention study; estimates are model-based rather than a prospective intervention trial.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: PubMed source abstract and Wiley publisher record (PMID 26843218; DOI 10.1111/ina.12285). No manuscript change was required.

Title: {Integration of a Coupled Fire-Atmosphere Model Into a Regional Air Quality Forecasting System for Wildfire Events}
Claim_Boundary: Integrates WRF-SFIRE one-way with AIRPACT and evaluates two wildfire events against fire perimeter satellite plume height and nearby PM2.5 observations. Forty-eight-hour simulations ran in under three hours; performance was mixed across cases and metrics. Supports concentration/air-quality forecasting feasibility without universal superiority.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: Frontiers open-access full text (DOI 10.3389/ffgc.2021.728726). No manuscript change was required.

Title: {Investigating the Spatial and Temporal Limitations for Remote Sensing of Wildfire Smoke Using Satellite and Airborne Imagers During FIREX‐AQ}
Claim_Boundary: FIREX-AQ comparison of airborne eMAS and GEO/LEO imagers quantifies near-source spatial and temporal limitations: GEO mean AOD can agree when resolution is finer than plume width but maximum AOD can be strongly underestimated; LEO sampling is daily. Supports the manuscript's satellite coverage/revisit/resolution limitation statements within this setting.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: AGU/Wiley open full text (DOI 10.1029/2023JD039085). No manuscript change was required.

Title: {Low-cost sensor network for wildfire monitoring and air quality measurements at remote community locations.}
Claim_Boundary: Supports prototype feasibility for remote monitoring and communications; large-scale incident performance and health-decision effectiveness remain unvalidated.
Audit_Note: Underlying publisher/DOI/official source was opened and the manuscript use was checked within the stated claim boundary.

Title: {Modeling Wildfire Smoke Pollution by Integrating Land Use Regression and Remote Sensing Data: Regional Multi-Temporal Estimates for Public Health and Exposure Models}
Claim_Boundary: Develops AOD and land-use-regression models for urban and rural ambient PM2.5 during a 2015 transboundary wildfire episode in southern Alberta. It supports spatially resolved outdoor exposure surfaces but does not incorporate individual mobility time activity indoor infiltration occupation or protective behaviour.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Partial correction required. Source route: MDPI open-access full text (DOI 10.3390/atmos9090335). The corresponding manuscript wording/attribution correction was applied: Rewrite the health-interface paragraph to distinguish area-level ambient concentration/exposure surfaces from personal exposure; cite filtration evidence separately for indoor mitigation.

Title: {Multi-Agency Ensemble Forecast of Wildfire Air Quality in the United States: Toward Community Consensus of Early Warning}
Claim_Boundary: Describes the real-time HAQES ensemble combining three US federal wildfire-air-quality forecasts and evaluates weighted ensemble performance including bias false alarms and hit rate. Supports classifying it as a concentration/air-quality forecast and early-warning system in its evaluated US context.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: AMS publisher full record and indexed article text (DOI 10.1175/BAMS-D-23-0208.1). No manuscript change was required.

Title: {Predicting hourly PM2.5 concentrations in wildfire-prone areas using a SpatioTemporal Transformer model.}
Claim_Boundary: Develops a multi-head-attention SpatioTemporal Transformer for hourly PM2.5 at Greater Los Angeles monitoring stations and evaluates abrupt wildfire-related increases. Supports metric-specific retrospective forecasting claims; it does not establish between-station fields cross-region generalisation or prospective warning performance.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: PubMed source abstract and Elsevier publisher record (PMID 36436649; DOI 10.1016/j.scitotenv.2022.160446). No manuscript change was required.

Title: {Prescribed Burns as a Tool to Mitigate Future Wildfire Smoke Exposure: Lessons for States and Rural Environmental Justice Communities}
Claim_Boundary: Uses the GEOS-Chem adjoint to estimate how prescribed burning could mitigate population-weighted wildfire-smoke exposure across western states and rural environmental-justice communities for the 2018 and 2020 seasons. It supports distributional consequences of land-management intervention but not the manuscript's detailed list of communication access household resources and response-capacity constraints.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Partial correction required. Source route: AGU/Wiley publisher full record and NOAA repository abstract (DOI 10.1029/2022EF003468). The corresponding manuscript wording/attribution correction was applied: Move this citation to a separate sentence about how prescribed-burning choices redistribute downwind smoke exposure; leave the detailed response-capacity list to sources that evaluate those constraints.

Title: {Spatiotemporal prediction of fine particulate matter during the 2008 northern California wildfires using machine learning.}
Claim_Boundary: Uses ten-fold cross-validation to select among eleven statistical algorithms and 29 predictors for daily PM2.5 during the 2008 northern California wildfires. Supports retrospective metric-specific concentration prediction and the need to report evaluation design; it does not establish live forecast performance.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: PubMed source abstract and ACS publisher record (PMID 25648639; DOI 10.1021/es505846r). No manuscript change was required.

Title: {Wildfire smoke exposure during pregnancy and perinatal, obstetric, and early childhood health outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.}
Claim_Boundary: Systematic review of 31 studies reports suggestive evidence linking pregnancy wildfire-smoke exposure particularly late-pregnancy exposure with reduced birthweight and preterm birth while calling for more homogeneous studies. Supports cautious association language rather than causal or universally established effects.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported with wording boundary. Source route: PubMed source abstract and University of Western Australia repository record (PMID 37931734; DOI 10.1016/j.envres.2023.117527). No manuscript change was required.

Title: {Modelling daily fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and wildfire effects using machine learning and deep learning in a cold urban region}
Claim_Boundary: Compares RF LSTM and XGBoost for daily PM2.5 at three Edmonton-area stations using R2 correlation and RMSE. Test performance declines and models underestimate unusually high wildfire peaks; XGBoost performs best in this dataset. Supports context-dependent comparison and extreme-event degradation rather than universal model-family superiority.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: Elsevier publisher full record and indexed author abstract (DOI 10.1016/j.apr.2026.103099). No manuscript change was required.

Title: A novel drone design based on a reconfigurable unmanned aerial vehicle for wildfire management
Claim_Boundary: No evaluated fire-plume task. General reconfigurable UAV design and payload discussion without a fire-plume sensing or response evaluation. Citation is retained only for the bounded contextual statement and is not counted as primary synthesis evidence.
Audit_Note: Underlying publisher/DOI/official source was opened and the manuscript use was checked within the stated claim boundary.

Title: Critical review of health impacts of wildfire smoke exposure
Claim_Boundary: Critical review finds consistent respiratory morbidity evidence growing all-cause mortality evidence mixed cardiovascular evidence and insufficient evidence at that time to identify specific susceptible subgroups. It supports health-review positioning and cautious susceptibility discussion but not unqualified claims that every listed subgroup was conclusively established by this review alone.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported with wording boundary. Source route: PubMed/PMC open full text (PMCID PMC5010409; DOI 10.1289/ehp.1409277). The corresponding manuscript wording/attribution correction was applied: Qualify the related-review table as covering evidence on potential susceptible populations; retain specific older-adult and cardiorespiratory statements only alongside later systematic evidence.

Title: Tracking hazardous aerial plumes using IoT-enabled drone swarms
Claim_Boundary: Reports a small indoor classroom prototype using compressed-air canisters whose propellant produced detectable CO. A drone swarm adjusted horizontally to repeated CO releases and searched plume boundaries after about 30 refinement experiments. The paper did not test chlorine and did not validate an outdoor emergency deployment or vertical tracking.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Correction required. Source route: NSF Public Access Repository accepted manuscript and IEEE DOI record (PAR 10180563; DOI 10.1109/WF-IoT.2018.8355118). The corresponding manuscript wording/attribution correction was applied: Replace chlorine-plume wording with controlled indoor CO-plume prototype and state the two-dimensional small-drone and airflow limitations.

Title: Unmanned aerial vehicles and low-cost sensors for air quality monitoring: A comprehensive review of applications across diverse emission sources
Claim_Boundary: Review filters 94 studies across diverse emission sources and synthesises UAV and low-cost-sensor capabilities calibration reliability spatial-temporal coverage rotor effects and regulatory limitations. Supports adjacent mobile-air-quality context and related-review comparison; it is not an end-to-end wildfire-response review.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported with scope boundary. Source route: Elsevier publisher abstract and indexed full-text preview (DOI 10.1016/j.scs.2025.106409). No manuscript change was required.

Title: Stationary and drone-assisted methane plume localization with dispersion spectroscopy
Claim_Boundary: Demonstrates chirped-laser dispersion spectroscopy with stationary and drone-mounted retroreflectors for controlled methane releases. The mobile configuration localized the source within plus/minus 1 m and estimated low leak rates within plus/minus 30 percent under an assumed Gaussian stability class. Supports the stated configuration-specific adjacent-domain result only.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported with scope boundary. Source route: Elsevier publisher record Princeton research portal and OSTI record (DOI 10.1016/j.rse.2023.113513). No manuscript change was required.

Title: NOAA’s HYSPLIT atmospheric transport and dispersion modeling system
Evidence_Role: External authority/context; not primary synthesis evidence
Claim_Boundary: Describes the development features and applications of HYSPLIT for trajectories transport dispersion transformation and deposition. Supports positioning it as a technical dispersion-model framework; it is not a wildfire-specific validation study.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: NOAA Air Resources Laboratory system page and AMS publisher record (DOI 10.1175/BAMS-D-14-00110.1). No manuscript change was required.

Title: Evaluating DIY air cleaner variability and potential for post-construction emission of aromatic VOCs during wildfire events
Claim_Boundary: Supports controlled performance and practical cautions for this construction protocol. It does not establish population health benefit or field effectiveness across designs and homes.
Audit_Note: Underlying publisher/DOI/official source was opened and the manuscript use was checked within the stated claim boundary.

Title: PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR): Checklist and Explanation
Evidence_Role: External authority/context; not primary synthesis evidence
Claim_Boundary: Introduces the PRISMA-ScR checklist with 20 essential and two optional reporting items for scoping reviews. Directly supports the manuscript statement that the review is reported using PRISMA-ScR guidance; it does not convert the review into a prospectively registered systematic review.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported. Source route: PubMed source record EQUATOR Network guidance and PRISMA official page (PMID 30178033; DOI 10.7326/M18-0850). No manuscript change was required.

Title: Framing governance for a contested emerging technology: insights from AI policy
Evidence_Role: External authority/context; not primary synthesis evidence
Claim_Boundary: Analyses 49 AI policy documents and identifies competing governance frames including technological self-governance government regulation stakeholder participation and international coordination. It supports discussion of framing and high expectations for public engagement. It does not by itself establish privacy redress lifecycle controls or that governance mechanisms generally lag rhetorical commitments in every jurisdiction.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Partial correction required. Source route: Oxford/Policy and Society publisher record and Nottingham repository manuscript (DOI 10.1080/14494035.2020.1855800). The corresponding manuscript wording/attribution correction was applied: Keep this source for policy framing and participation; rely on dedicated guidance for privacy traceability redress and lifecycle-control claims and soften claims about top-down marginalisation or implementation gaps.

Title: Multifidelity prediction in wildfire spread simulation: Modeling, uncertainty quantification and sensitivity analysis
Claim_Boundary: In a canonical wildfire-spread scenario control-variate and multilevel Monte Carlo strategies provide up to 100-fold speedup versus standard Monte Carlo while quantifying aleatoric uncertainty and rate-of-spread sensitivity to weather and fuel parameters with WFDS. Supports the active computational-cost statement but not smoke chemistry concentration or health prediction.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported with scope boundary. Source route: Elsevier publisher abstract and Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya repository full text (DOI 10.1016/j.envsoft.2021.105050). No manuscript change was required.

Title: An overview of autonomous vehicles sensors and their vulnerability to weather conditions
Claim_Boundary: Reviews adverse-weather effects on automotive cameras LiDAR RADAR ultrasonic sensing GNSS and communications. Supports the general claim that precipitation and fog can degrade optical sensing but transfers from road vehicles rather than wildfire UAV deployments and should not be used for an uncited exact 50-percent figure unless tied to the reviewed underlying experiment.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported with transfer boundary. Source route: MDPI/PMC open full text and PubMed record (PMCID PMC8400151; PMID 34450839; DOI 10.3390/s21165397). The corresponding manuscript wording/attribution correction was applied: Retain only the qualitative active wording and do not restore the deleted exact visibility-loss percentage.

Title: A scoping review of wildfire smoke risk communications: issues, gaps, and recommendations
Claim_Boundary: Used for scope comparison or evidence synthesis; primary-study claims are checked against underlying evidence where material.
Audit_Note: Underlying publisher/DOI/official source was opened and the manuscript use was checked within the stated claim boundary.

Title: AI Governance: A Challenge for Public Health
Evidence_Role: External authority/context; not primary synthesis evidence
Claim_Boundary: Transferred governance context; not fire-specific validation and not counted in the 562-report primary corpus.
Audit_Note: Underlying publisher/DOI/official source was opened and the manuscript use was checked within the stated claim boundary.

Title: FIRE-VLM: A Vision-Language-Driven Reinforcement Learning Framework for UAV Wildfire Tracking in a Physics-Grounded Fire Digital Twin
Claim_Boundary: Supplies a possible source, perimeter, rate-of-spread, or routing input; it is not direct evidence of pollutant concentration mapping or health protection.
Audit_Note: Underlying publisher/DOI/official source was opened and the manuscript use was checked within the stated claim boundary.

Title: Assessing the 2023 Canadian wildfire smoke impact in Northeastern US: Air quality, exposure and environmental justice
Claim_Boundary: Supports improved mapping and exposure estimation for the studied June 2023 episodes. It does not establish prospective operational performance, causal environmental-justice effects, health outcomes, or generalisation to other fires and regions.
Audit_Note: Underlying publisher/DOI/official source was opened and the manuscript use was checked within the stated claim boundary.

Title: Ethics and governance of trustworthy medical artificial intelligence
Evidence_Role: External authority/context; not primary synthesis evidence
Claim_Boundary: Multidisciplinary review identifies data quality bias opacity safety/security and responsibility attribution as trustworthiness issues in medical AI and proposes transparency traceability human responsibility whole-process review and multi-stakeholder assessment. Supports general governance context but not validation of fire-response safeguards or crisis-consent mechanisms.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported with transfer boundary. Source route: BMC/Springer open-access full text (DOI 10.1186/s12911-023-02103-9). No manuscript change was required.

Title: How does evacuation risk change over time? Influences on evacuation strategies during accidental toxic gas releases
Claim_Boundary: Develops a modelling framework combining dynamic toxic-gas risk assessment and agent-based evacuation simulation to assess how risk and strategy change over time. Supports agent-based heterogeneous evacuation scenario modelling as adjacent hazardous-release evidence; it does not support Bayesian or Monte Carlo health-risk inference and is not fire-specific.
Audit_Note: Verification result: Supported with scope boundary. Source route: Elsevier publisher abstract and indexed article record (DOI 10.1016/j.ijdrr.2024.104531). The corresponding manuscript wording/attribution correction was applied: Retain only the agent-based evacuation use in the revised paragraph; keep the Bayesian and Monte Carlo statement generic or support it with another appropriate source.
